title: Kernel swap + backfill crib notes
content:
context: quick personal checklist + notes for doing a kernel swap on GPU hosts and backfilling running capacity if nodes go out. this is a working crib — messy. keep to basics during shift.

TODAY FOCUS
- finish kernel swap on rack-7B (10 nodes) during low-traffic window 02:00-04:00 PST
- test backfill automation on canary pool (canary-pool-1) before broad roll
- confirm failover paths for running Dedicated customer jobs

PRE-FLIGHT (30m before)
- check tracing dashboard: /console/latency/top-routes -> ensure <1% p99 spike in last 30m
- list nodes to touch: label=rack=7B, gpu-type=A100-40GB, kernel-current=6.1
  command: kubectl get nodes -l rack=7B -o wide | grep A100
- open a channel in #infra-ops: "marcus/kernel-swap-rack7b" and ping oncall
- verify spare-capacity: pool spare-gpu-count >= 6 (we need 5 spare for buffer)
  quick check: ./scripts/pool-capacity --pool dedicated-rack7b --spare

SWAP STEPS (one node) — follow exactly
1) cordon node and drain (graceful)
   - kubectl cordon <node>
   - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
   - check running pods and note long-lived Dedicated pods (customer tags)
2) snapshot local logs and nv cache in /var/log/gpu-sys/ -> scp to temporary bucket
3) reboot to maintenance kernel: sudo systemctl isolate rescue.target || sudo reboot --boot-loader-entry="maintenance-6.4"
   - WAIT: watch console for kernel panic messages — keep serial capture
4) after reboot, validate drivers and nvidia-smi: nvidia-smi -L && nvidia-smi topo -m
5) run small perf smoke: python tests/smoke_infer.py --model small-embed --iters 3
6) rejoin to cluster: kubectl uncordon <node>
7) sanity checks: node ready, kubelet logs <5 warnings, gpu memory visible to pods

BACKFILL PLAN (if capacity drop > threshold)
- threshold: if available-gpu < 4 then trigger backfill
- backfill sequence: (a) move preemptible workloads to cold-pool; (b) spin up burst-capacity in us-west-2-b; (c) route new incoming requests to hosted fallback model (gpt-small-v1)
- commands:
  - move: ./scripts/migrate-preemptibles --from dedicated-rack7b --to cold-pool --max 8
  - spin: terraform apply -var 'burst_count=6' infra/burst_pool || ./tools/burst-up --count 6
  - route: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/route/update -d '{"policy":"fallback-hosted"}'
- notify CS if Dedicated customers affected: message template in #cs-ops/Templates/backfill-alert

QUICK TROUBLESHOOTING NOTES
- if drivers not binding after kernel: check /lib/modules/<kernel>/nvidia. often missing dkms build; run: sudo dkms autoinstall && sudo depmod -a
- hung kubelet: systemctl restart kubelet; if not, capture systemd-journalctl -u kubelet --since "1 hour ago" > /tmp/kubelet-journal.log and escalate
- network flap after reboot: check iptables + bonding state: ip a; cat /proc/net/bonding/bond0
- if node goes NotReady > 10m, flag urgent and trigger fallback route immediately

METRICS TO WATCH (during ops)
- cluster-wide free GPU count (grafana: infra/gpu/free-count) target >= 5
- scheduler pending pods (k8s pending) < 3 for > 5m
- hosted p99 latency for text-gen routes not to exceed baseline+30%

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs (post-shift)
- refine backfill automation to prefer warm-pools in same AZ first (latency reasons)
- add smoke test for A/B quant profiles after kernel swap (see PR 319)
- follow up with SRE on more robust serial-console capture tooling (current script flaky)
- note: adjust canary size to 2 nodes next run to get better signal

SNIPPETS / COMMANDS I KEEP FOR MYSELF
- list nodes by kernel: kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,KERNEL:.status.nodeInfo.kernelVersion | grep 6.1
- drain w/wait: kubectl drain $N --grace-period=120 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --timeout=7m || true
- quick pool free count: python -c "from infra import pool; print(pool.get_free('dedicated-rack7b'))"

NOTES TO SELF
- don't iterate on automation during active rotation — only run tested scripts
- keep CSR template handy for any customer impact messages
- breathe if things go sideways, call for backup early (Priya usually available)

END-OF-SHIFT CHECKLIST
- confirm all nodes in rack7B are back to Ready and labelled kernel=6.4 when complete
- post a short summary in #infra-ops: what was changed, any customer hits, follow-ups
- file a short retro note in confluence with screenshots and perf graphs (link below)

REFERENCES:
- playbook: confluence:Infra - Live Kernel Swap Playbook
- related jira: INFRA-7421 (kernel-swap automation)
- pr: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/319
